answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to hold a long, time-locked stake that only grows through work verified by unrelated peers. A newcomer starts as a bare tundra figure with no weight; each epoch it must complete fresh tasks, earning a mesa of accrued credit whose releases are spaced out. A zephyr of clones funded from one source shares one deposit, so splitting adds no weight while each duplicate still pays lock-up cost. Weight is thus proportional to provable, spread-out history rather than key count.
